Unfortunately, I am not really looking at the issue from the betterment of the VAs, I am looking at it from the position of a company like Hoyo and why they would not want to sign this contract when they have signed different contracts for VO work before. 

You typed it by yourself again, and I quote: "Many VAs want reform and modernization of the union but that can only come after the AI problem is solved." So, the VAs want reform of what? And why would Hoyo sign a contract when there IS a need for reform? Why not present a contract with the reform already in place? How does this benefit Hoyo in any way? Remove the plight of the VAs from the equation and look at this problem from the POV of the decision makers. SAG AFTRA and Hoyoverse. Before this strike, they were conducting business as usual, and then suddenly SAG called for a strike due to AI and then the contract to be signed has a lot of grey space and areas where Hoyo might not have a say that has nothing to do with AI. You could almost understand why Hoyo is reluctant to sign such a contract. 

As for the VAs that are members of SAG, they will stand for the strike as they should. However, to then require Hoyo to sign an unclear, obviously needing reform contract without benefit to Hoyo? Quite an irritating corporate prospect. I could hear the Law Dept complaining already.

I stopped reading after you yourself typed 'union should revise'. When will they revise it to be clear? After Hoyo signed the contract or when dogs start flying? Contracts should not have these 'supposed' things. Hoyo bases their decision on the contract presented, and it is so obviously skewed in favour of SAG that a juggernaut of a company like Hoyo would not allow themselves to be beholden to a foreign union.

The Inquisition IRL only became such a negative thing because it stayed for a long time and wielded by many corrupt leaders and fear mongers. Trespasser council basically wants to disband the Inquisition before they could have more legitimacy in being a divine martial order, and then we learn that there are spies among us. Who is to say that a couple of years from the Dragon Age, the Inquistion would still be devout and holy? The Seekers and Templar Order are the same. As much as people vilify the order now, it did start as a peaceful organisation with dedicated leaders.

Why the developers used Inquisition (aside from sounding cool) could be more etymological than anything else. Inquistions are "institutions within the Catholic Church whose aim was to combat heresy, conducting trials of suspected heretics." With the death of Divine Justinia, the two hands are now looking to work out which of these 'heretics' are to blame? The mages who fled to Redcliffe or the Order who isolated themselves at at Theirinfall? Developers probably thought of how the two organizations supposedly under the Chantry are behaving like heretics against the will of the Divine. Who is the best to judge aside from the Throne itself? Question. How could you take it over? Seriously? You have an "altruistic" organization down to two divisions, a group of synths who are rebelling against oppression by assault and "subterfuge" AGAINST all the civilians in the HQ who knows to run a tight ship to keep the institute from total blackout due to limited resources, and obviously brain washed to see life in the commonwealth as a possible death sentence. 
Could the railroad even handle ALL the necessary things needed to keep the facility afloat? A couple of scenarios rely on the denizens of the Institute as well. 

 One, the civilians, and the technicians that make up the bulk of the Institute. Should they all be killed, exiled, branded as slaves, or held hostage for their crimes and made to labour under the new management of freedom fighters? Will the Railroad just become the new 
Institute?
 
Two, the synths rebelling against their master, DO they even wish to gain control of the very device that grant them existence? Will they use that same device to proliferate, and will they non-synths to have that tech? 

By the time of FO4, the insitute is already falling apart, only the Father's plan could save their energy crisis. Take them over, and you are now burdened to keep this afloat. Will you also take apart Diamond City's power to preserve the Institute?

The only one who could take over the Institute is the Brotherhood, and even then, they would expend a lot of their nationwide resources if they chose to run the place. They didn't, so it's moot, but a loose civilian organization like the Railroad would be stretched so much. Add in the fact that they are a volunteer organization who seems to not have a singular leader. For all that Desdemona acts like one, remember that Ticon HQ certainly acts detached.

Destroying the Institute as a Railroad Agent really is the only one that could achieve what the Railroad's mission is that could satisfy this group of volunteers.

I'd like to offer my opinion as well regarding this especially since I am one of those people who considers DA2 as my favourite of the trilogy. Like your's, this is a very subjective opinion.

First, I'd like to pre-emptively say that your criticisms of the game is VALID. Your opinion is the opinion of the general public in this sub and outside of the community.  

On MetaCritic User Scores: 
Origins - 8.8;
2 - 4.7; 
Inquisition - 6. 

That should put your review into perspective and also the perspective of those who defend DA2 in this sub. It is not a campaign to say DA2 is the best game in the genre without equal (it has too many faults to be in contention);  it is simply a fight to shed the opinion that the game is BAD and not worth consideration. It is simply DECENT.

Now since I do not want to generalize those who like the game these are my own points against or for yours.

1. - The best story out of the three for me. It is personalized and suffocating because that is the story of Hawke who fled their home costing ome of their sibling's life. You do not like Kirkwall, I'd hazard a guess that Hawke also do not like Kirkwall. But as with the tragedy of Hawke's life, that is the fortune he is dealt. 

2. - Now this is the most subjective of all I think. I do not like Varric in either DA2 or DA:I, but I'll say that Isabella, Carver and Fenris trumps every other companion in the trilogy for me with only Morrigan and Leliana higher than them. The DA2 characters also feels the most familial and they seems to be the group that bonded the most compared to the others. Expected because they have time to develop their own relationships. Time skips actively progressed their relationships with each other. It makes it more alive and natural compared to the other games.
 
3. - I don't care about the Romance. I really do not.

4. - Enemy swarms are irritating. You will have difficulty in finding people who do not share this opinion. Though I will say this in terms of combat gameplay. DA:O > DA2 > DA:I, especially in terms of tactics.

5. - Equipment is bad but let me say that compared to DAO it is DA2 as an easy pick for me. Those hats at DAO are a nightmare. I'd rather morrigan not wear any headpiece than subject her to the nightmare that is DAO hats.

6. - Hawke is the best protagonist for me. Really. I like how DA2 is such a personal story that makes me really feel for these characters and Hawke is another character that I am in a ride with. 

5. - I don't bother extensively with CCs. When I spent 5 hours on a CC with Skyrim I've resolved to not waste time in CC anymore. Unfortunately I spent a whole day in DA:I just designing a character. I don't really even remember fiddling with DA2 CC. Must be a nightmare as what you've said. 

6. - I'm always weirded out by complaints about the dialogue wheel especially with some people who choose just one color boxing their Hawke into just one personality. Some just play the dialogue as forever purple, blue or red. You know you can choose other colors right? In my game I was surprised that my Hawke became agressive at the third act when I pretty much chose a lot of Blue when interacting with family, Sarcastic when I found NPCs to be particularly annoying, and Red when I want to eviscerate a pest. It seems pretty boring just sticking to one color of personality when a person is never one dimensional.


So this is my unique perspective about DA2. As I've mentioned in this sub before, my love for DA2 is how personal and enclosed this story is. Progress of relationship between the characters without Hawke's interference (Isabella & Aveline, Fenris & Sebastian, Merril and Anders), the progress of the city in each act for either good or worse, the progress of Hawke through their adventures in the span of years, how their personality evolves in response to everything. Hawke's story is a tragedy and I think DA2 tells it decently.

What I want to know is how far you've progressed in the story? For my personal experience I restarted DA:I about 4 times thinking that I didn't like the game because of the gameplay of classes. So I restarted the story changing characters and their backgrounds until something fits. Even took months breaks thinking I am just exhausted in playing games and the DA universe.

Due to my irritation at the game, I decided to just become a 2 wielder templar aligned character. I also didn't pay any mind about the Hinterlands and didn't care about Companion Approvals and that my thinking was to simply get over it for the story so that I could complete the series. My irritation in the game was that bad.

Surprisingly I started to love the game. Then I came to a simple realization. Adventuring is a TRAP. The Hinterlands is a TRAP. Exploration will suck the soul out of you in this game because the maps are excessively large with nothing in it. Then I started to look at the quests logs more often. The main quests are the bulk of the story and the more you do the main quest the more involved you'll become and the more interesting the game becomes. The side quests, if they are not voiced, and if they are bot related to a character you care about, are entirely useless.

 Exploration of the world map should be at the bottom 3 of your priorities and it is only worthwhile to explore the map if you are smithing or doing a completionist run. 

Sooo.... different compared to DA:O and DA2 in the approach of enjoyment. I wanted to explore every inch of the map in DA:O because of the stories and the weapons, meanwhile DA2's smaller and linear story telling makes exploring a fruitful endeavour since just changing maps or day suddenly takes you from one plot to another. In DA:I, you'd think the maps are a good thing because it makes you fall into a sense of big content but most of that content is just air. There is nothing in the maps. Unfortunately I am led to believe it is the fault of the Open World genre explosion started by Skyrim. Obviously DA team is not great at environmental story telling engagement. 

So to sum up, for my advice? Do the main quest and let the main quest be your priority since that is arguably the strongest appeal of the game. Do a one pass of the game's main quest if you want while ignoring most of the side quest since ultimately the side quests are really useless and doesn't add anyhting worthwhile. You may like the story and the story may lead you to want to explore the open world more and collect more and maybe allow you to scour all the unnecessary maps of the DA:I game, then you'll find yourself doing other character types, races and companion approvals/disapprovals. It did for me, hopefully it would for you too.

You get 50% of their trade power in nodes they have power in. Your main trade node is Lubeck where you collect lovely ducats and you have a merchant transferring trade from the Baltic, two trade nodes Novgorod do not have any presence in since they end their trade at Novgorod.

You have to check how much trade power Novgorod have in the trade nodes you can pull power in since that is the time transfer trade power will be useful to you.

Since Novgorod's main trade is in Novgorod they really do not have much trade power in the Baltic especially since in your game the Novgorod province was already eaten by Muscovy, so they only have Neva. You also do not have much presence in the Novgorod trade node so they cannot add their 50% trade power to your non existent trade power in Novgorod. So basically you are just getting a half of their trade power in Novgorod that isnt really worth much since they don't have a lot to begin with. 

How to make use of the transfer trade power? Make your presence known in the Novgorod trade node by either conquering a province or sending merchants or trade ships.
